title: Progressive hedging timeout sash and tenant-fairness controller (hosted 5xx mitigation)
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Summary: Multiple mid-market customers escalated recurring, tenant-scoped waves of 5xx and long tail timeouts over the past two weeks. Symptom pattern: upstream frontdoor receives client retries (SDK and partner LB), fanout to hosted runtime causes KV cache eviction and kernel scheduling contention; certain request shapes hit slowpath and time out -> amplified client retries -> tenant-level failure. Goal: implement a protective runtime shim that (1) applies progressive hedging with a timeout sash to avoid synchronized retry storms, and (2) enforces a tenant-fairness controller to prevent single tenants causing host-wide KV thrash. Deliverables: runtime policy, SDK guidance update, emergency runbook, monitoring dashboards, and a targeted hotfix for affected regions.
impact_summary: Affected 4 paying customers with visible user errors and degraded latency; internal SLO breach for hosted-api.us-west-2 for three 15-minute windows. Potential revenue impact if unresolved; escalations opened by Customer Success demanding hotfix. Root cause hypothesis verified by trace sampling: repeated client-side retries within 200-500ms window coinciding with tenant upload spikes.
technical_notes: Observability: correlation IDs show identical request payload fingerprints replayed 6x during surges; KV cache eviction rates spike immediately before 5xx wave
Slowpath trigger: requests with early/long context-switching (large prompt + streaming) are hitting an unoptimized attention kernel on certain model variants
Network interaction: frontdoor/edge timeouts differ from runtime timeouts which causes asymmetric retry behavior
Existing mitigations tried: lowered SDK default retries for 2 customers (manual), edge circuit-breaker raised for tenant X (temporary relief), pre-warming of KV cache (limited effect)
decisions: Implement a progressive hedging policy in the frontdoor-to-runtime path: start with single hedged probe at 320ms, escalate to full hedging for requests older than 1s
Add a ‘timeout sash’ at the proxy layer: align frontdoor and runtime timeouts and inject a canonical idempotency header to allow safe fast-fail
Introduce tenant-fairness controller that tracks per-tenant in-flight token consumption and enforces admission caps under pressure
Prioritize a minimal hotfix (canary) for us-west-2 before global rollout
Update SDK docs and temporarily publish recommended client retry settings until runtime is updated
tradeoffs: Progressive hedging reduces tail latency but increases peak work; mitigated by the fairness controller admission caps
Shorter timeouts improve recovery speed but may increase client-visible failures; we'll pair with clear CS comms
Admission caps risk throttling aggressive but legitimate tenants; we'll tune by percentiles and offer override for Dedicated customers
implementation_steps: A. Frontdoor change: implement hedging probe generator and timeout sash (ENG frontend team) - estimate 3 pts
B. Runtime change: tenant-fairness admission controller + telemetry export for in-flight token counts - estimate 4 pts
C. SDK guidance: patch docs and release note discouraging default aggressive retries - estimate 1 pt
D. Canary rollout: us-west-2 then eu-west-1 with 2% traffic -> 20% -> 100% if metrics stable
E. Runbook: add fast rollback path and customer comms templates
qa_plan: Unit tests for hedging timer and sash behavior
Integration test: synthetic replay harness that simulates 6x client retry bursts and measures KV eviction and 5xx rate
Load test under mixed-tenancy with admission caps enabled to verify throughput degradation bounds
Canary validation: monitor 95/99/99.9 latency and 5xx delta, automated rollback if 5xx increases > 0.5% absolute
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: per-tenant in-flight tokens, KV eviction/sec, hedging-trigger-rate, hedged-success-rate
Alerts: sustained hedge-trigger-rate > 5% of requests AND 5xx increase > 0.2% -> immediate rollback
Tracing: sample traces to include hedging decision metadata and idempotency header for correlation
